evidence.note: New per-package floor file; header documents the regeneration command `bash tests/coverage.sh --update-floor`, which matches the actual --update-floor branch in tests/coverage.sh.

Verified consumer of the floor file: internal/fsm/* and workflows require every statement covered; all other packages are compared against their floor line, and packages with no floor line are reported as 'no floor' but not enforced. The 28 floor lines cover every non-fsm package except internal/version, which is const-only (no statements) and therefore never appears in the merged profile.

Assertion lowered to 'invalid git base'. Verified against internal/gitcontext/gitcontext.go:305,319,327 which now emit lowercase 'invalid git base: ...'; the pre-branch base commit 61ffdf72 emitted 'Invalid git base'. grep is case-sensitive, so the test update is required, not cosmetic, and it still fails if the message regresses.
Confirmed all three error sites were lowercased consistently (ST1005 style), so no other shell assertion in tests/ is left matching the old capitalization.

findings.note: The floor lines are pinned to the exact measured percentages (e.g. internal/learnsource 70.8, internal/contextpack 76.1) with no slack, so any sub-0.1% coverage drift fails the gate. tests/coverage.sh mitigates this by exporting the go.mod-pinned GOTOOLCHAIN, and --update-floor refuses to lower a line without --allow-floor-decrease, so this is an accepted tightness rather than a defect.
